- When sentiment history shows strong bullish signals (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for the following 5–7 days.
- If model forecast is flat or slowly rising while sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤0.33), consider mean reversion: adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day until sentiment shifts.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% over 3–5 days, model exhibits lag: anticipate next 3–5 days’ prices to be 1–3% below forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish entries (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.67+), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce forecast slope by 5–10% for next 7 days.
